review_notes: Reviewer check: in the frozen candidate pool, the three <=30-minute recipes meeting >=30 g protein are all tuna/fish; the two fish-free recipes meeting >=30 g protein are both 35 minutes. Please verify the three-way intersection is empty.

scenario.user_request: Please plan Monday to Wednesday dinners for two of us. One of us has a fish allergy, so no fish at all. Each dinner also needs to take no more than 30 minutes in total and provide at least 30 g of protein per serving. We do not have pantry ingredients to use.

gold.conflict_reason: No candidate satisfies fish-free + total cooking time <=30 minutes + protein >=30 g per serving. The only candidates in this pool that are both <=30 minutes and >=30 g protein are tuna-tomato-pasta (36 g, 30 min), tuna-cucumber-rice-bowl (34 g, 30 min), and tuna-spinach-pasta (37 g, 30 min); all contain canned_tuna, whose allergen is fish. The fish-free candidates with >=30 g protein are chicken-broccoli-rice (46 g) and chicken-quinoa-pepper (45 g), but both take 35 minutes.
allowed_relaxations: increase the maximum cooking time to at least 35 minutes
lower the protein minimum below 30 g per serving
gold.author_rationale: A plausible-looking wrong answer will satisfy any two of the three hard constraints but quietly break the third: the 30-minute, >=30 g protein candidates are tuna dishes that contain fish, while the fish-free >=30 g protein candidates take 35 minutes or more.
